searchText: hi guys we are looking for the ways to measure SGX overhead of EVMC execution -> has anybody tried that? <@!425274498732916736> , <@!425279588009246720> would you have availability to present EVMC to the Flashbots team? No, but I know there exists Graphene-ng project which allows executing unmodified linux binaries in SGX. What exactly is to be presented? Just maybe talk about EVMC and how it abstracts state and whether it can work with witnesses and how it can potentially run in SGX and how it compares with performance to Go EVM more like a casual Q&A session and intro <@489256758989029405> yes, sure, I can do this. let me try to arrange, would <@!425279588009246720> be available too? Sure, sounds interesting. Not entirely clear what benefit SGX brings here though? 😉 iiuc, running in the evm in SGX will help protect flashbot users from having their transactions stolen by flashbot mines (among other things?) how is it enforced that they are always run within an sgx enclave? don't users still need to trust those who run the nodes, given there's no "sgx signature" attached to eth1 blocks from within sgx? or perhaps i'm not sure i understand the term stolen in this context. does it refer to frontrunning or soemthing else? I think there some scheme where the SGX enclave assembles a block (ensuring the MEV is paid out) and it spits out a header to mine. After a valid POW is found, the SGX module would share the block body Stolen as in the flashbots network gives miners an MEV transaction where some split goes to the miner and some split goes to the finder. A miner *could* just repackage the MEV tx and take all the fees. With SGX, the tx could be encrypted when it reaches the miner Ah so you mean some kind of mining pool controlled by flashbots where the pool is run on sgx not to give out too many details?
